canonical_question: How does the '60–80 nm' size of the spherical precipitates compare to the 500 nm sub-grain size in terms of volume fraction contribution?

question_variants.question: How does the '60–80 nm' size of the spherical precipitates compare to the 500 nm sub-grain size in terms of volume fraction contribution?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text provides the size of spherical precipitates (60–80 nm) and mentions sub-grain boundaries, but does not provide a sub-grain size of 500 nm or a calculation of volume fraction contribution.

answers.answer: The text confirms precipitates are 60–80 nm and dispersed along intergranular boundaries, but contains no data on a 500 nm sub-grain size or volume fraction calculations.
answers.boundary_limitation: No sub-grain size or volume fraction data provided in the text.
evidence_spans: The attained results clearly demonstrated that the macrostructure and phase composition of samples produced by LPBF were similar to those obtained by its counterpart AMF alloy.
In both cases, the alloys were composed of a single solid-phase solution with a BCC crystal structure with similar lattice parameters, as expected according to Kang et al.
In terms of microstructure, both alloys showed differences in the distribution of tungsten and an increased amount of vanadium at grain boundaries.
